title: Introduce ephemeral session-map + migrate IO layer to SQThread for incremental cache compaction
creator: Ravi Patel
description:
Background: Our continuous-batcher workload is repeatedly contending on the global session registry and the legacy libaio-backed IO adapters. This increases tail latency during spikes and makes incremental compaction work (background KV grooming) brittle. Goal: introduce a lightweight ephemeral session-map (lock-free fastpath for active sessions) and migrate the IO layer for compaction/priming to a dedicated SQThread submission queue model. This reduces global lock contention, simplifies scheduler wakeups, and lets the compactor perform small, low-latency IO without blocking the main batch control plane.

Scope:
- New ephemeral session-map implementation (per-core shards, RCU-style retirement) and adapters for existing session lifecycles.
- SQThread IO shim that exposes batched submission/completion semantics tuned for small writes/reads used by incremental compactor and warmup bridge.
- Replace the compactor's blocking IO path with SQThread calls; add backpressure signal between compactor and batcher.
- Upgrade the low-level IO dependency to liburing v3.x where SQThread depends on newer kernel features; bump related build deps.
- Telemetry: add session-map contention metrics, compactor latency histograms, and handoff counters.

Why different from prior work: Earlier tickets focused on lease/epoch coordination and prefetch pipelines; this ticket targets the hot path where short-lived session operations and compacting IO meet. The ephemeral session-map is intentionally lightweight to avoid the heavy-weight lease protocol in fast-path request routing.
acceptance_criteria:
1) No increase in p99 token latency for steady-state QPS (target: <= +2%).
2) Reduction in global session-registry lock contention metrics by >= 60% under representative benchmark.
3) Compactor median IO completion latency <= 5ms on CI kernel with SQThread.
4) All new code covered by unit tests and integration test harness that reproduces previous contention pattern.
5) Successful canary rollout to runtime-2.3 canary pool with automatic rollback on SLA breach.
plan:
Phase A (design + prototyping, 1 sprint): design data structures, RCU-safe retire path, SQThread API surface; prototype in a feature branch.
Phase B (implementation, 2 sprints): implement ephemeral session-map, adapter layers for registration/unregistration, SQThread shim and small compactor refactor. Add metrics and feature flag.
Phase C (bench + CI, 1 sprint): run stress tests, perf harness (the 'kv-hotkey-thrash' scenario), validate kernel features in CI images.
Phase D (canary + rollout, 2 weeks): enable on canary runtime hosts, monitor telemetry and failover behavior, migrate remaining compactor instances, and flip default flag on release if stable.
risks_mitigation:
- Kernel/dep mismatch: maintain fallback to the existing libaio adapter behind a feature flag; smoke test preflight checks during startup.
- Regression in session semantics: keep a compatibility adapter that converts ephemeral registrations back to legacy lease heartbeats during canary.
- Increased GC pressure from ephemeral structures: use epoch-based reclamation and tune retire batches; add leak detectors.
- Unforeseen compactor latency spike: enforce rate-limiter and a token-bucket on compactor queue to protect batcher SLOs.
rollout_steps:
1) Merge behind feature flag and run internal perf jobs.
2) Deploy to staging with liburing-enabled kernel images.
3) Canary deployment (5% hosts) for 72h with automated SLO checks.
4) Expand to 50% if green; run full-scale ramp test.
5) Promote to runtime-2.3 GA and monitor the first 48h closely.
6) If any metric breach, disable flag and roll back compactor changes only (compactor can be switched back to libaio path).
qa_tests:
- Unit tests for ephemeral session-map correctness (concurrent register/unregister).
- Integration test reproducing previous contention pattern and validating reduced lock holds.
- End-to-end perf harness with synthetic traffic: megabatch/short-session mix.
- Chaos test: rapid session churn and compactor-induced IO bursts.
- Regression test for compactor correctness after SQThread migration.
- Nightly stress job comparing p50/p95/p99 vs baseline for 7 days.
